issues.description: The header declaration in ray_sphere_intersect.h uses the function name check_sphere_hit(...), while the implementation in ray_sphere_intersect.cpp defines ray_sphere_intersect(...). main.cpp calls ray_sphere_intersect(...) (via the included header), so the declaration/definition name mismatch will cause compilation errors (missing/incorrect prototype) and confusion about which symbol to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function declaration and definition use the same name/signature. Either change the header declaration to declare ray_sphere_intersect(const float*, const float*, const float*, const float) or rename the implementation to check_sphere_hit to match the header. Also ensure all callers (main.cpp) and includes use the same function name. This will restore correct compilation and prevent confusion about the API.

issues.description: The header in example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h (template) declares a function named check_sphere_hit(...) while the implementation and all call sites use the name ray_sphere_intersect(...). The solution repository uses ray_sphere_intersect consistently. This mismatch between the template header and the implementation/usage is an unintended identifier naming inconsistency that will confuse students and causes compilation/ linkage errors (call site and implementation names differ from the declared prototype).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the header declaration in example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h with the implementation and usage by renaming the prototype to: bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius); This makes the header, implementation, and call sites consistent (matches the solution).
